# Replicating the Offense-Defense Gap Analysis Specifically for AI-Assisted Social Engineering in Cybersecurity Contexts

**Problem:** Potter et al.'s offense-defense gap analysis covers technical capabilities. Social engineering (phishing, pretexting, vishing) represents a distinct AI capability category where the offense-defense asymmetry may be even larger.

**Direction:** Analyze AI capabilities for offensive social engineering (spear phishing generation, pretexting scripts, vishing voice synthesis) vs. defensive social engineering detection (phishing classification, social engineering training content). Measure AI uplift for each side using available tools. Compute the social-engineering-specific offense-defense ratio.

**Why it matters:** Social engineering is often the entry point for technical attacks. If AI dramatically increases social engineering offense capability without equivalent defensive uplift, the actual attack surface expansion is larger than technical benchmarks suggest.

**Relevant context:** Potter et al. arXiv:2504.05408; vibe hacking extortion case; Microsoft threat actor AI abuse report Apr 2026.
